request: Analyze GSE235942 for PMID 37996046 (A comparison of bone microarchitectural and transcriptomic changes in murine long bones in response to hindlimb unloading and aging.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

factors.sex: paper analyses males; GEO also holds female controls

final.primary_estimand: Effect of disuse (hindlimb unloading) and of aging on tibial gene expression; no exercise intervention (ABS.p2, S2.1.p1)
planned_contrasts: 4mo HLU vs control (Fig 5A/G; from a prior study, not in this series)
final.paper_results: No DEG counts stated in text; volcano plots only (Fig 5G-I). Exercise is mentioned only as a general countermeasure (S1.p1, S4.p8).

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Paper compares hindlimb unloading (disuse) with aging in male C57BL/6J mice (ABS.p2, S2.1.p1). DE: limma on kallisto counts, threshold raw p<0.05 & logFC>|1.5| (S3.3.p2). No exercise, training or loading arm anywhere in methods or Table 1; 'exercise' appears only in Introduction/Discussion as background (S1.p1, S4.p8).

checks: GEO tissue marrow-flushed tibia, BioJupies processing, C57BL/6 ages 6/22 months match S2.1.p1/S2.4.p1

ownership.reasoning: Data availability statement S2.6.p1 deposits RNA-seq under GSE235942; metadata matches the paper's tissue, ages and HLU treatment.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (A1, AM1, YM3, ...) equal the metadata 'description' field for all 30 samples (inspect alignment_keys). Derived formula-safe columns treatment, age, sex.

matrix.reasoning: All values integer (integer_fraction 1.0), median 11, max 2.6e6; data_processing: 'raw counts per Sample' from BioJupies. kallisto estimated counts rounded by BioJupies; type not in doubt for the gate since the case stops at design.

candidates.reason_rejected: Hindlimb unloading is disuse, the opposite of exercise; it does not identify an exercise effect

design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast: the series contains only control and hindlimb-unloaded (disuse) mice at 6 and 22 months (paper S2.1.p1, GEO treatment column control/HLU). Neither disuse nor aging can stand in for an exercise effect, so the requested estimand is not identifiable.
design.reasoning: The requested estimand (effect of exercise) has no arm in this study. Running HLU vs control and relabelling it as exercise would invert the biology; the paper itself frames exercise only as background (S1.p1, S4.p8).

discrepancies.paper: male mice analysed; 4mo HLU group from a prior study
discrepancies.data: GEO also holds 7 female 22mo/6mo controls and 3 male 22mo HLU samples not described in the paper; no 4mo samples
